8. Learned Advocate in support of his submissions, relied on the case of Kaimuddin Shaikh alias Kaimu Shaikh vs Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Rajshahi, 3 BLC 410, the case of Jobayer Hossain vs Noor Hafez, 56 DLR (AD) 22, the case of Rafizuddin Ahmed vs Mongla Barman, 43 DLR (AD) 215, the case of Waziul Bashar (Md) vs Khaja Ahmed, 6 BLC 124, the case of Jabed Ali vs Abu Sheikh, being dead, his heirs Md Naimuddin, 1983 BLD (AD) 1=35 DLR (AD) 31, the case of Tajuddin vs Moktar Ahmed, 1991 BLD (AD) 144, the case of Farhaduzzaman vs Abdul Hasem Hawlader, 2 XP 81. 

 13. Decision cited by petitioners, particularly the cases of 56 DLR (AD) 22, 43 DLR (AD) 215, 1983 BLD (AD) 144, speaks that 'Even a trespasser's possession is good and valid against the entire world except the true owner and such possession is entitled to protection until he is evicted by due process of law.' We have also seen that long user of the suit land plaintiffs acquired a right of possession as such, he cannot to be thrown out of possession until and unless defendant could prove that they have better title over the land of plaintiffs by instituting properly constituted suit. 

 14. Decision cited by the learned Advocate Mr Shihab Uddin Ahmed, accepting the case of Rafizuddin Ahmed vs Mongla Barman, 43 DLR (AD) 215, the case of Dewan Shamsul Abedin, Mutwalli of Dewan Aftebur Reza Chowdhury Waqf Estate, 13 MLR (AD) 163, the case of Belayet Hossain vs Nurul Alam Mir; 42 DLR (AD) 20, other decisions cited are not to be considered as in front of the Hon'ble Appellate Division's decision, the decisions of High Court Division should not be required to be looked into. The decisions as cited by the learned Advocate for the defendant if we consider in particular perspective then also these decisions support plaint case as in all these decisions it is held that for permanent injunction as regard dispute landed property the relief is available to a person who is in possession. The court may inquire incidentally into the respective claims of the parties to the suit for determining whether the plaintiff is in possession of the disputed property and are entitled to the specific relief of permanent injunction. 42 DLR (AD) case is a case on granting temporary injunction. Article 144 of Limitation Act provides 60 years possession to give title, over the land of Government. We have seen that Appellate Court did not disturb the finding of trial court's finding of plaintiffs' possession for 70 years. We find merit in the rule.
